findings.summary: An obsolete source-open rejection clears the newer selection loading guard.
findings.evidence: renderSelection catch unconditionally sets this.loading=false; deferred failure regression observes false while replacement open is unresolved.
findings.fix: Fence failure publication by revision and retain unavailable/loading state until the matching source is committed.

findings.summary: Returning A->B->A while B opens can take the last successful A fast path and let obsolete B replace the native source.
findings.evidence: lastSelectionKey changes only after source commit; same-key branch does not invalidate the pending render. Reproduction ends with model server and Captured-browser.mts.
findings.fix: Reserve attempted selection identity before I/O; latest selection must retire older work.

findings.summary: Close followed by Open in the same extension skips recreating the source because the selection cache survives owned-tab closure.
findings.evidence: close sets opened=false but retains sourceUri/lastSelectionKey; regression observes zero native source tabs after reopen.
findings.fix: Invalidate reader presentation caches when closing, retaining only durable model state.

findings.summary: A missing current source retains the previous current-understanding claim.
findings.evidence: readBaselines only replaces successful reads; failure reports an error while projectStudy still counts the old baseline as current.
findings.fix: Represent unavailable current source explicitly; preserve historical choices but withhold current-understanding claims until source verification recovers.

findings.summary: State/README documents still say learner UI and progress are not implemented.
findings.evidence: Current implementation and native history checks exist in the uncommitted tree; prior pending prose has not been reconciled.
findings.fix: Update cycle/state/usage documents with current bounded evidence and review/native-visual limitations.

findings.summary: Missing Close-during-acquisition regressions allow pending Open or Run to recreate owned resources after Close completes.
findings.fix: Add deterministic deferred-initialization and deferred-controls.start tests, then fence or drain these acquisitions with the reader lifecycle. A completed Close must prevent an earlier Open from recreating panels and an earlier Run from starting a runtime afterward.
findings.evidence: open() executes "await this.initialize()" before unconditionally setting "this.opened = true; this.closing = false" (112-114); action(run) awaits controls.start then unconditionally calls service.start (144-145). close() drains only this.rendering/library writes after sampling currentRecord (208-210). In-memory execution of the current TypeScript with deferred boundaries reproduced openedAfterLateCompletion=true and two panel creations after Close; a deferred UI Run called service.start once after Close. studyWorkspace.test.ts has only retirement and source-drift tests; nativeStudyRunner.ts closes only after state.cleaned. E6.5 explicitly requires close during open.
findings.test_stub: test('closing during initialization does not reopen the study', async () => { /* Arrange a deferred initialization in the reader boundary harness. */ const opening = reader.open(); await reader.close(); initialization.resolve(); await opening; assert.equal(reader.inspect().opened, false); assert.equal(panelsCreatedAfterClose, 0); }); test('closing during service startup prevents a late study run', async () => { const starting = reader.action('run'); await startEntered; await reader.close(); serviceReady.resolve(service); await starting.catch(() => undefined); assert.equal(runtimeStartCalls, 0); });

findings.summary: The first understanding command can persist a browser source revision under the server item; all existing tests initialize the reader before marking.
findings.fix: Add a cold-reader regression with persisted browser selection and invoke codebook.markUnderstanding before Open/attach. Resolve the default participant together with the selected source after initialize, while preserving explicit outline item/hash arguments.
findings.evidence: understand defaults "participant = this.selection.participant" before "await this.initialize()" (194-195). initialize restores progress.selection (229), and the later write combines the pre-initialization participant with "sourceHash ?? selected.source.hash" (199). Current-source in-memory execution restoring browser during initialize recorded savedItem=server with the browser hash. workspaceHarness always calls reader.attach before returning (studyWorkspace.test.ts:28), and nativeStudyBootstrap marks only after open-paused. The advertised Toggle Understanding for Selected Source command therefore has no cold-start identity test.
findings.test_stub: test('the first understanding command marks the restored browser item and its source', async () => { /* Arrange saved selection participant=browser and distinct server/browser hashes; construct without Open or attach. */ await reader.understand(true); const progress = await library.readProgress(); assert.equal(progress.decisions.at(-1)?.item, 'browser'); assert.equal(progress.decisions.at(-1)?.sourceHash, browserSourceHash); assert.equal(progress.decisions.some(decision => decision.item === 'server'), false); });

findings.summary: The declared 16-study and 1,000-decision retention boundaries have no regression coverage, including preserving updates at a full store.
findings.fix: Add at-limit and limit-plus-one behavior tests for both collections: reject a new study/decision without changing existing bytes, permit an existing study checkpoint and identical intent retry at capacity, and verify the writer lock is released after rejection. Add a small exact-byte/over-byte atomicPrivateWrite case instead of constructing large files.
findings.evidence: The new guards are "progress.decisions.length >= MAX_LEARNER_DECISIONS" (56) and "!existing.some(...) && existing.length >= MAX_LIBRARY_FILES" (76); atomicPrivateWrite rejects "Buffer.byteLength(bytes) > limit". E6.3/E6.5 explicitly promise count/size limits with no eviction. learning.test.ts uses at most two decisions and one archive, and its rename-failure test writes a tiny value below a 1,000-byte limit. Native cases also retain exactly one study. Corruption and rename tests do not exercise refusal at capacity or the important update/idempotency exceptions.
findings.test_stub: test('a full study library retains all history and still checkpoints an existing study', async () => { /* Arrange 16 distinct valid archives. */ const before = await archiveBytes(); await assert.rejects(library.saveStudy(seventeenthStudy), /library is full/); assert.deepEqual(await archiveBytes(), before); await library.saveStudy(updatedFirstStudy); assert.equal((await library.list()).length, 16); }); test('1,000 learner choices reject new intent but accept an identical retry', async () => { /* Arrange 1,000 valid decisions in progress.json. */ await assert.rejects(library.decide(newDecision), /history is full/); assert.equal((await library.decide(existingDecision)).decisions.length, 1000); assert.equal(await lockExists(), false); });

findings.summary: Source changes do not refresh the installed learning outline when the reader is closed.
findings.fix: Publish the accepted baseline/progress projection or fire the tree invalidation after every successful baseline update, independently of opening the reader; keep native source rendering conditional. Verify the outline refresh event while opened is false.
findings.evidence: The watcher calls 'this.readBaselines().then(() => this.renderSelection())' at line 407 (the document-change branch does the same at line 403), but renderSelection line 311 returns for '!this.opened'. close line 213 sets opened=false while the outline remains registered. The only 'this.treeChanges.fire(undefined)' is in publish at line 306. Consequently an outline that showed a current-source check can keep displaying that check after the source changes, even though inspect().model already reports reviewNeeded. The existing source-change test checks only the model and replaces EventEmitter.fire with a no-op.

findings.summary: The close docstring still promises panel disposal although the new lease branch deliberately retains the reader panel.
findings.fix: Describe closing frame delivery/listeners and releasing an external lease, with panel disposal limited to an internally owned viewport. Keep the ownership distinction explicit in this lifecycle entry point.
findings.evidence: The motivating comment says 'Disposes only the owned panel during run cleanup'. The added branch at lines 122-125 instead executes 'this.record('viewport.lease-released'); this.lease.released(); return;' without calling panel.dispose; panel.dispose occurs only at line 127. Retaining the external reader is the explicit Cycle 6 ownership contract and is covered by the new leased-viewport test.

findings.summary: StudyObservation is a new exported type alias with no consumer.
findings.fix: Remove the unused alias; retain observationSchema and the existing StudyArchive-derived types actually used by capture, persistence, and presentation.
findings.evidence: Line 32 declares 'export type StudyObservation = z.infer<typeof observationSchema>;'. Repository-wide rg for the complete symbol, excluding generated dist and node_modules, finds only this declaration; no implementation or test imports or references it.

findings.summary: Each source-derived edit retains another full source document and opens another non-preview native tab; neither Close nor disposal prunes the documents cache, so one source editing session grows without the study/decision limits.
findings.fix: Keep a replaceable source-derived reader separate from immutable observed-source URIs, coalesce baseline change events, and bound/cache only currently needed or open captured documents; release obsolete cached entries when their owned tabs close and when the reader is disposed.
findings.evidence: The watcher and document-change handlers call readBaselines().then(() => renderSelection()) (lines 402-408). Each changed source hash enters the URI and documents.set(uri.toString(), source.text) (323-324), then showTextDocument uses preview:false (329). No documents.delete/clear exists, including close/dispose (205-218). A causal harness using the current transpiled StudyWorkspace methods with native APIs stubbed performed 100 distinct approximately 8 KiB source-derived revisions: 100 non-preview source opens, 100 cached documents, 821290 retained text bytes, and 100 cached documents still after close. This is method-level retention evidence, not native-tab or timing QA.

findings.summary: Archive write latency blocks live pause selection and source/context refresh: refresh awaits checkpoint before following the current pause or rendering, and checkpoint awaits saveStudy plus listing even after its archive is already captured.
findings.fix: Separate the bounded/coalesced archive writer from live projection refresh. Publish/follow committed in-memory evidence without waiting for disk writes, report save status separately, and await the writer only at explicit final-checkpoint/retirement boundaries. Add a deferred-save regression proving a later pause and control status still render before storage is released.
findings.evidence: refresh executes await this.checkpoint(this.service, record) before selection.follow and renderSelection (258-264); checkpoint assigns activeArchive at 276 but waits for library.saveStudy/archive listing at 277. Concurrent refresh calls return the same pending promise (255). The control finally block also awaits refresh before its final publish (160). A causal harness using the current methods with saveStudy held pending observed archiveAlreadyCaptured:true, renderCount:0, selectedStudy:null; releasing that save produced renderCount:1 and selectedStudy:instance_record. Native effects/capture provider were stubbed. This establishes UI update dependency on storage, not an observed real-disk latency or blocked MCP protocol call.

findings.summary: Switching an item from the keyboard in Source-linked flow loses focus during the loading transition and never restores it to the originating flow control.
findings.fix: Capture the focused control/region before hiding selected content and retain that focus token across loading messages. Restore it only when the matching completed selection is visible, unless the user deliberately moved focus; alternatively keep navigation controls outside the hidden data region. Add a flow-button -> loading -> loaded focus regression alongside the existing moment-focus test.
findings.evidence: D6.2 says a new pause preserves keyboard focus and D6.5 says updates preserve focus. studyClient executes "element('selected').hidden = message.loading" at 72, but reads document.activeElement only later at 90-91 and then tries to focus a rebuilt flow button inside the hidden region at 96. The actual generated context HTML was exercised with Playwright CLI against the existing deterministic QA host: focus #flow button[data-item=browser], Enter, qaPublish(loading), qaPublish(history). Result: before BUTTON/browser/flow; during BODY; after BODY; focusPreserved:false. Evidence: artifacts/cycle-0006/review/pass1-design-focus.txt. This reproduces the webview loading/focus defect; it does not assert native editor visual acceptance. Existing 22-check QA only verifies moment focus on a non-loading update.

findings.summary: Two saved-study selections are resolved by the first completed read, so an earlier choice can silently discard the learner's latest choice.
findings.fix: Reserve a selection-request generation when the history message is accepted, before readStudy starts; show the loading state immediately and apply only the latest requested study after I/O. Keep the displayed revision check for incoming stale messages separate from the generation used to arbitrate accepted pending selections.
findings.evidence: receive(history) awaits "this.library!.readStudy(message.studyId)" (444) before any invalidation, then checks "message.revision !== this.revision" (445). The first completed read calls renderSelection, which increments revision at 317. Two valid messages A then B therefore share the old displayed revision: if A finishes first, B is discarded despite being the latest intent. A deferred-read harness executing the current transpiled receive method reproduced latestRequestedStudy=B, finalSelectedStudy=A, latestIntentPreserved=false. This occurs before source rendering and is distinct from the already reported renderSelection A-B-A race. Archives can contain tens of MiB, so the pending read is a real interaction boundary.
findings.test_stub: test('the latest saved-study choice wins even when the earlier read finishes first', async () => { /* Arrange two deferred archive reads and one current displayed revision. */ const first = receiveHistory(studyA); const latest = receiveHistory(studyB); readA.resolve(archiveA); await first; readB.resolve(archiveB); await latest; assert.equal(reader.inspect().view.model.selection.studyId, studyB); assert.equal(renderedSourceHash, archiveB.observations[0].source.hash); });

findings.summary: Selection from moments, source-linked flow, or Follow current never updates the native learning outline selection, leaving two different selected items visible.
findings.fix: Synchronize the visible outline to the committed model participant using TreeView.reveal with select:true and focus:false, provide getParent for the flat roots, and synchronize on visibility when the outline is hidden so background updates do not unexpectedly open it. Cover flow/moment selection and automatic current-pause changes without stealing keyboard focus.
findings.evidence: select updates "this.selection = { ...this.selection, participant: ..., follow: false }" (189), and refresh changes participant for Follow current (262). publish only assigns "this.outline.message" and invokes "this.treeChanges.fire(undefined)" (305-306). getTreeItem keeps stable item IDs (382), and there is no outline.reveal or other programmatic tree-selection operation anywhere in the implementation. Thus clicking Server in the native outline and then Browser in a webview changes the source/context model while retaining the native Server selection. Context7 official TreeView documentation and installed @types/vscode distinguish readonly selection/programmatic reveal from the tree-data refresh event. This is source/API evidence, not a claim of native pixel verification, and differs from the existing closed-outline progress refresh finding.
findings.test_stub: test('selecting the browser moment synchronizes the native outline without moving focus', async () => { /* Arrange visible outline selected on server and focus in the moments webview. */ await dispatchReaderMessage({ type: 'select', revision: currentRevision, participant: 'browser' }); await settledReader; assert.deepEqual(tree.selection, ['browser']); assert.equal(reader.inspect().view.model.selection.participant, 'browser'); assert.equal(focusedRegion, 'moments'); });
